title: Deduplicate cross-region retry fan-in causing overcount in per-model rolling charts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We are seeing consistent, small but material overcounts in per-model rolling charts (24h / 7d) for a subset of customers routed through our multi-region rate-limit proxies. Root cause investigation shows the telemetry stream is receiving duplicate token events when client retries (SDK or client-side) are proxied through different regional gateways and later merged during ingestion. Each retry instance arrives with a different proxy_region provenance but identical request_id and overlapping token offsets, resulting in fan-in duplication across shards and elevated per-model totals in the Console.

Why this matters:
- Console-facing per-model and tenant charts are used for billing validation and operational alerting; overcounts cause customer confusion and support escalations.
- The duplicates inflate both token counts and token-cost attributions for models with long streaming responses (prefix caching cases are particularly affected).

Investigation notes (what we've validated):
- Grafana dashboards (metering-proxy.latency, ingest.duplicates.count) show correlated spikes aligned with global rate-limit events on 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-09. (See dash: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/metering-overview)
- Telemetry samples show identical request_id + tenant_id + model_alias + token_offset ranges arriving with different proxy_region fields.
- Sharded ingest pipeline dedup logic currently keys by request_id only after shard routing; because proxy_region differs, duplicates land in different shards and do not collide for deduplication window.
- Replaying a sandbox trace through a single-shard ingest demonstrates dedupe would have prevented the double-count.

Proposed changes (short):
1) Canonicalization at edge: attach a canonical global event key computed as sha256(request_id || tenant_id || model_alias || token_offset_range) and include it in the event envelope before proxying between regions. This gives downstream a consistent dedupe key.
2) Ingest-layer cross-shard dedupe index: add a compacting redis-backed recent-key index (TTL 120s) that dedupes identical canonical keys even if they land on different shards.
3) Adjust dedupe heuristics: require token_offset overlap >= 80% and arrival delta <= 60s to avoid collapsing legitimate retries that advanced the stream.
4) Backfill plan: conservative correction job that compacts duplicate events for rolling windows in the past 7 days for affected tenants; we will run with read-only dry-run first and publish reconciliation notes to billing team and affected customers.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Edge canonicalization reduces downstream work but requires SDK/edge release and may miss older clients; fallback dedupe at ingest is required.
- Cross-shard index adds an operational dependency (redis cluster) and could be an availability surface during bursty traffic. To mitigate, index is best-effort: if unavailable we fall back to current behavior and emit telemetry.
- Aggressive dedupe heuristics risk undercounting if genuine retries include new tokens. Our overlap/time thresholds are conservative to prioritize correctness over aggressive compaction.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): Deploy ingest-layer dedupe with index enabled for 5% of ingestion partition ranges and monitor delta between raw and deduped counts. Create dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/def456/dedup-canary.
- Stage 2: Enable edge canonicalization for internal SDKs and Redwood-verified proxies; continue ingest dedupe as defense-in-depth.
- Stage 3: Run backfill correction for affected tenants in waves (1% customers per wave) after validation. Publish reconciliation reports and offset corrections to billing pipeline.

Monitoring / success criteria:
- deduped_token_count delta < 0.5% baseline after full rollout for non-affected tenants; >95% reduction in duplicate-reporting for previously impacted tenants.
